Based on the 100 experiments and general NAS-Bench-201 structure, these are the patterns I expect to hold:

- **Bad parents gain most.** Swapping in a convolution helps far more when it replaces a parameter-free op (`skip_connect` or `avg_pool_3x3`) on the same edge. Cells built only from those ops perform badly, so they have the most room to improve.
- **Missing node0→node3 shortcut.** Adding a skip on edge 3 helps much more when edge 3 is currently `none`.
- **Path loss.** Removing an edge (or replacing a conv with pooling) is especially harmful when the input–output connectivity already hangs on few paths. Losing edge 3 or edge 0 is then catastrophic.
